general_information.Description: The Graduation Thesis is an integrative experience that brings together various components of the undergraduate international business studies in a more applied setting and under a new perspective. It enables students to further their knowledge and skills in international business and related topics which they have found to be especially interesting or beneficial to them. As part of the course, students will learn about all aspects of the process of developing and carrying out the graduation thesis and gain an understanding of standards and expectations needed to successfully complete their dissertation. This thesis project will be completed by a group of 3-5 students, however each student will defend the thesis individually in front of a thesis committee. Each group of students will be supported by a supervisor, who will provide them with essential guidance in conducting a research, writing a thesis in a formal format and defending their arguments in front of the examination board. The thesis' topic is concerned with such areas as (1) international business strategies, (2) contemporary issues of cross-cultural business management, (3) global entrepreneurship, (4) global human resource management - current practices and future trends, (5) FDI in Vietnam, (6) ethical issues in international business, (7) international trade in the current global geo-political landscape and (8) international business practices towards sustainability
general_information.StudentTasks: (1)Choose the project within the selected concentration (2)Divide and schedule work (3)Attend all scheduled meetings with supervisor (4)Produce document and product according to project requirement (5)Defense individually work in front of examination board

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: The students would be able to identify topic background, topic relevance, relevance of research question, overview of dissertation structure.
The students would be able to conduct an appropriate literature review and review of literature related to the research question.
The students would also be able to clearly state the gap in literature with respect to research questions and with selected theoritical models.
The students would be able to understand and apply methods used to collect data, data collection methods, sample characteristics, limitations of the research project
The students would be able to design and implement appropriate qualitative and/or quantitative methods
The students would able to systematically present the data before interpretation.
The students would be able to analyse the data and do discussions of findings relatively to the literature review
The students would be able to answer to the research question, explain the relevance of answer to practice and make recommendations
The students would be able to understand what Harvard referencing is and how it would correctly be applied during the process of dissertation
The students would be able to understand deeply the necessary steps to carry out a research project and to write a structured report/dissertation.

The students would be able to implement and possess their own project in the application to all types of business model.
The students would be able to be confident with their final product of dissertation which could be used to apply on solving the real practical problem of the business world

assessments.Duration: According to deadlines by the Academics Department
assessments.No Question: One piece of written work of no more than 100 pages
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Combination of all relevant acquired knowledge, and research and written skills
assessments.Grading Guide: Evaluation is based on the format, presentation of data, insightful analysis & practical recommendations for the research problems

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: • Report 1: Introduction and Thesis Outline • Report 2: Literature Review and Theoretical models • Report 3: Methodology, Data Analysis & Findings • Report 4: Conclusions and Recommendations
assessments.Grading Guide: • Based on the schedule in the syllabus, each group report will be evaluated by the group supervisor. This evaluation is called progress assessment. • Individual mark for each progress assessment report is decided by the group supervisor and is assessed on the basis of the actual contribution by that individual to the group report. The individual mark can be lower or higher than the group mark and is in the range from 0% to 120% of the group mark where the average score of group members cannot be more than group mark.
assessments.Note: Completion criteria: Mark of each report must be >=4/10 All four personal progress assessment reports account for 24% of the whole Thesis with weights - Report 1: 6% - Report 2: 6% - Report 3: 6% - Report 4: 6%

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Combination of all relevant acquired knowledge, and research and presentation skills
assessments.Grading Guide: • Presentation mark is given by each member of referee committee for each student on final project presentation. This personal mark is the average of all member of referee committee. • Total presentation time for each group is 30 mins. Each student must make his or her own presentation.
